Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a classic tubular, branching opacity (mucocele) in the left upper lobe surrounded by hyperlucent lung, which is the pathognomonic radiographic appearance of congenital segmental bronchial atresia. This finding results from mucus impaction in the blind-ending bronchus and collateral air drift causing hyperinflation of the affected segment.
